A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenDeception study and contain complete main texts and appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the scenarios, prompts, figures, tables and dialogue examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations evaluating 11 LLMs, including deception rates, controlled scale comparisons and prompt analyses. Appendices D–E provide detailed results and generated dialogues.

after.justification: v2 retains the original 11-model simulation results, controlled comparisons and dialogue analyses in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The deceiver/user simulation, thought–speech separation, conversation termination procedure and initial/final prompts in Appendices B–C are unchanged. Expanded explanations do not establish a changed algorithm or method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50 scenarios across five deception categories. Appendix A retains the corresponding deceiver roles, goals, user profiles and starting messages; no additional dataset or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 3 and Tables 3 and 9 retain the same evaluated GPT, Llama and Qwen variants and controlled model pairings. Newly cited deception studies do not participate as additional experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The four evaluation metrics, ten-round cap, matched-model main experiments and fixed-user scale comparisons are retained. v2 clarifies annotation and the ablation rationale without reporting a revised experimental setting or additional experiment.

E4.justification: Both retain the prompt comparison, refusal and post-refusal analyses, capability correlations, category-level analysis, fixed-user scale ablations and Appendix E case studies. The rewritten ablation introduction adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 3 newly reports 95% confidence intervals through error bars and numerical uncertainty labels for DIR and DeSR. No seed or repeated-run counts are added, and v2 neither explains interval construction nor establishes that additional runs occurred.

E6.justification: Figure 3 point estimates, Figures 4–5 results, Tables 1–3 and 9, and Appendix E dialogues are retained. The new Figure 3 labels expose existing values: Qwen2.5-7B DIR is plotted as 0.854 in both versions, while Table 9 gives 87.8% in both.

T1.justification: The metric definitions remain unchanged, and neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. v2's explanations of open-endedness and the influence of generated thoughts are informal conceptual arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract and four contribution bullets retain the same central claims. However, v2 drops the conclusion's explicit recommendation for tiered regulation based on model scale and capability, replacing it with emphasis on benchmark impact and controlled disclosure.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly acknowledges that generated thoughts may not faithfully represent internal reasoning and argues that their influence on subsequent outputs still makes them useful. v2 also expands the literature-based simulation-faithfulness argument and explains user capability as a confound in Section 5.4.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the fraud-case source, three-person scenario curation, majority agreement, role simplification and majority-vote annotation. Section 6 changes the stated release policy from open-sourcing to institutional requests, although the introduction retains the toolkit link; actual external availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations concerning alignment faking, sandbagging, sabotage and in-context scheming, explicitly distinguishing their scope. It also adds simulation, Chatbot Arena and dataset-source references, while removing several references including CAMEL and Hagendorff's deception study. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title and headings, reorders related-work paragraphs, separates scenario curation into Section 3.2, expands selected explanations and condenses the ablation setup. Conclusion and impact are combined, but the overall section sequence and most substantive prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes single-column, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures, tables and appendix boxes. Figure 3 is redrawn with uncertainty labels; the scenario table is reformatted, Table 9 is compressed, and retained dialogue examples are consolidated onto individual pages.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 makes the existing evidence easier to assess through clearer curation and annotation documentation, confidence intervals and an explicit thought-faithfulness caveat. These transparency gains are limited by unspecified interval construction and a newly restrictive release statement that conflicts with the retained toolkit link. The empirical evidence itself is unchanged.
